utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina. et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. A special welcome to you Ambassador Paro, I do understand, and Mr. Cule, a special welcome to you. The Chamber highly appreciates that you were able to attend this hearing, although notice had been given only yesterday evening that we intended to have this hearing. That's highly appreciated. Before we go to the substance of this hearing, I first want to establish that Mr. Cermak is present. Mr. Cermak, yesterday, we briefly discussed that counsel would not be there but you were all in agreement that we could proceed even in the absence of counsel. I see you're nodding yes, so that's on the record. I also see that Mr. Gotovina and Mr. Markac are not present in court. Let me just see. I should have received two notices, I will get them on my screen so that I can look at them. Here I have a form, absence from court due to illness, although it's not about illness, that stating that Mr. Gotovina has discussed the matter with his counsel, that he understands that he has a right to be present but that he waives this right. And on the second page, unlike yesterday, there's no further explanation of the present situation. Mr. Misetic, would you like to add anything or would you just leave it as it is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can just confirm that we have discussed it and the circumstances from yesterday remain unchanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that you are still instructed to participate in any hearing on procedural matters, as are scheduled for this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mikulicic, let me just check the other form. Same form. The box that Mr. Markac has discussed the matter with counsel is ticked. The waiver box has not been ticked. There are no further comments on the second page. Mr. Mikulicic, would you like to add anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's not much to add. I had a telephone conversation with my client this morning, and he is in the same position as he was yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just checking whether all the information I should have and sometimes comes in only one or two minutes before the hearing, whether I've seen it all, and that is what takes me a second. Yes, then, having dealt with these formal matters, the Chamber has received a response filed by the Prosecution, a response to the written motion, the motion to issue a subpoena for -- in order to ensure the attendance of Mr. Brammertz on the hearing on the 16th of December. That is, next week, Wednesday. As I said before, the Chamber wants to focus primarily on the requests to freeze the present situation, and -- but, is, of course, is looking forward, also, because the matters are not entirely unrelated to what we could expect on the 16th of December. Now, it was suggested by the Gotovina Defence that Mr. Bajic would be in the delegation which would represent the Croatian government on Wednesday. You may have seen that. I do not know whether you have already considered the composition of the delegation for next Wednesday. If so, we'd like to hear now already who will be on the delegation. Could you please activate your microphone when you speak. Yes, Mr. Paro.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am the Ambassador of the Republic of Croatia, and my government has furnished me with a written statement. However, I can answer immediately that my government is not opposed to the presence of Prosecutor Bajic to the hearing on the 16th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and -- then, Mr. Bajic, is it the intention of your government to make him a member of the delegation or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: Well, according to what I said, we have nothing against that so he has to be approached and then he would know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we invited primarily, of course, the government to appear and not individuals; although, it has been suggested that we could do so. But, of course, if you have already the intention to -- for him to be on the delegation that represents the Republic of Croatia on Wednesday, then, of course, no further action would be even to be considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: So -- if the Court wishes, you can invite him and we have no objections on that. I suppose that he would turn up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, I would invite you to -- perhaps to consult with -- perhaps it is you yourself who composes the delegation. Whether -- even without an invitation that he would be here anyhow because he would be a member of the delegation, that would save us even to consider to write him a letter and in what way to do that and how to communicate with him. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, stop me if this is not a helpful intervention, but based on my understanding of the thrust and purpose of the hearing of December 16th, it appeared to an inquiry into the results of the administrative investigations with specific focus on documents that were produced, documents that were not produced, documents that remain in dispute, in contrast to anything having to do with efforts by the judicial authorities or judicial investigation, and maybe that's a bit of the confusion here. I would have been surprised if anyone outside the administrative investigation would have been part of that process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, perhaps I should have informed the parties that the chamber is considering, at this moment, to extend the scope of that hearing. The matters, as I said before, are not totally unrelated, so therefore the Chamber is considering that and that's the reason why I'm inquiring in these matters. And apart from that, existence of documents, logic, we'd like to have as much expertise available as possible, and I do not intend at this moment to further elaborate on this matter, but I was just inquiring whether the Republic of Croatia had already made up its mind as far as the composition of the delegation is concerned. And the Chamber took note well of the observations made by the Prosecution in this respect in the submission of this morning, and we'll also consider whether that matter was something, although introduced in a motion, whether that was a matter which really was a response to what seemed to be the core of that motion; which was subpoena to be issued against Mr. Brammertz. But it can be understood, since that matter apparently as a side issue was introduced in the motion, so, therefore, it's understandable that you at least reacted, responded to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. This may be an opportune time, though, to advise the Chamber that we did also obviously review the Prosecution's response. We have, whenever the Chamber finds it convenient, and with your leave we would like to address some of the matters raised there, and in particular because I think it is related to what Mr. Tieger raised, which is whether is there is a connection between what the initial purpose of the hearing was on the 16th and our motion, and I think can explain that with the Chamber's leave at the appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, at this moment, we are focussing on a different matter, and I never had the impression that if you would be given an opportunity to respond to certainly these matters that you would remain silent, Mr. Misetic. We all too well know that are you only too glad to respond to anything said in that response. Mr. Ambassador, if you would have made up your mind as far as the composition of the delegation is concerned would you inform us. If that could be done this afternoon, that would be fine. If not, we'll consider what to do. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The hearing today was scheduled in response to a written motion filed by the Gotovina Defence, as I said before, which sought, through an order, to ensure the presence of Mr. Brammertz next week, Wednesday. This motion was followed by several oral motions mainly seeking cease and desist orders in various respects and the temporal scope of those orders was not limited, but in the alternative it was said that at least we should have a temporary order which would freeze the present situation, and that's the focus of hearing this afternoon. The Chamber thought it wise when the -- when it invited the Registry to get in touch with the representatives of the Republic of Croatia to very briefly set out what motions were filed, because, otherwise, we -- the Chamber feared that the representatives of Croatia would -- would not even know what they were called for. The letter in which an invitation is put on paper and a very short annex setting out with hardly any detail what the basis is will be filed, or is filed already, so that the parties will know under what terms the representatives of Croatia were -- what kind of information they received before coming to this courtroom. Now the factual background which is not set out in any detail in the annex to the letter is the following. That, already for some time, the Prosecution of Mr. Ivanovic for concealing and/or destroying archival material is the subject of -- has been the subject of motions and some decisions. The main topic in that litigation is immunity. Last Thursday, the Chamber was informed that -- by the Gotovina Defence, and I'm not giving any opinion about to what extent the information is accurate or not, but that Mr. Ivanovic had been deprived of his liberty. That was on Thursday. The Chamber was, yesterday, informed that he is not deprived of his liberty anymore at this moment. He was released yesterday. The Chamber further was informed that searches were conducted and material was seized, including computers, in the law offices in which the Gotovina Defence works, and also outside those law offices. That is to say, two computers that were in the possession of two members or former members of the Gotovina Defence team travelling to Zagreb, and that these two computers were seized as well. The specific concerns raised in this respect were a violation of legal privilege. That is, the privilege of confidentiality of communication between counsel and accused. Second issue which was raised was the risks that any of those materials seized would contain material which was under an order by this Tribunal to be kept confidential. These were the two concerns, in addition to the earlier litigated and that litigation has not yet finished, litigation about the immunity for Mr. Ivanovic, and the question whether he enjoys such immunity as a member of the Gotovina Defence team. Apart from the concerns expressed by the Gotovina Defence, in view of their work and the members of their team, the Markac defence brought to the attention of the Chamber that one of the members of their team allegedly had been, as it was said, discussed. I do not know exactly in what context and for what purpose. But, therefore, he joined in the concerns, although less specific and less concrete at that moment, expressed by the Gotovina Defence. The first thing the Chamber would like to hear is whether there are any factual updates to be made, in relation to the information the Chamber received yesterday. Is there anything, Mr. Misetic, you would like to bring to the Chamber's attention, updating us on the factual information?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, nothing, other than, as the Chamber is aware, there was supposed to be a hearing this morning in Mr. Ivanovic's case. That hearing did in fact proceed and is now completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Anything the Prosecution would bring to the attention of the Chamber from a factual point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I may have a few questions for the representatives of the Republic of Croatia. Yesterday during the hearing it -- it -- there was no -- no solid information about the searches and the seizures. The Chamber asked yesterday whether it was known in what context the searches had taken place. Could you inform us as who authorised -- authorised the searches and in what context they took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have before me a document which I believe addresses each of your questions, so if you will allow me, I would like to read it for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then we'll see whether we have any further questions. But perhaps we find the answers already in the document you will read. Now, it is our experience that if someone starts reading, that the speed of speech usually goes up which then causes problems for our interpreters and our transcriber. So if you read take your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: I will have mercy on the translators. [Interpretation] The Republic of Croatia cooperates with the ICTY, based on the constitutional law on cooperation between Croatia and the Tribunal dating back from 1996 and based on other regulations. The activities that are being taken place in view of complying with the requests of the ICTY Prosecution, so far we have complied with 853 such requests. We have complied with the order of the Trial Chamber dated 16th September 2008 to find the missing artillery logs pertaining to the military and police Operation Storm, or, rather, to establish its lot. As well as to finds the archival documents in the possession of the Republic of Croatia which is not stored in officially archives. In order to implement the order of the Trial Chamber dated 16 September 2008, so far, we have carried out an administrative investigation and the Trial Chamber and the Prosecutor's office have been informed in six detail reports, which provides explanation about all the measures an actions that have been undertaken within the scope of this administrative investigation. As a result of the administrative investigation, or, rather, since the results of the administrative investigation have found to be insufficient on the part of the Prosecutor's office, and after the meeting between the Prosecutor and the prime minister of Croatia in September 2009, a special inter-sectoral task force has been established. The task force is headed by the head office of the police. The main task was to eliminate any shortcomings and failures of the administrative investigation, and also to find documents that is sought only not by the OTP and the Trial Chamber of this Tribunal, but which are also sought by the Republic of Croatia to include them in its archives. [In English] Not to include them in its archives but -- because they are property of Croatian archives. [Interpretation] The task force has therefore drafted an action plan and an analytical information as its working documents and as the foundation for all the future actions. The task force has already submitted a report on its activities on the 9th of November, 2009. That report has been submitted to both the Trial Chamber and the OTP. In the course of any future actions, the task force has inspected documents in the operative administration of the armed forces of Croatia and the central military archives and the task force has found the documents which indicate the efforts of the Main Staff of the armed forces to collect, protect, put in order and prevent any misuse of documents pertaining to Operation Storm and also to Operation Flash. Those efforts are reflected in the initial order by the Chief of the Main Staff dated June 1998. The task force, in its actions, has come by certain information which represents the reasonable doubt as to the fact that certain individuals might have committed crimes which are prosecuted ex officio and that is why, on the 7th December, 2009, it was defined that police investigation would be carried out in compliance with Article 177 of the Law on Penal Procedure, as well as investigative actions in keeping with Article 211 through 215, of the Law on -- of the Law on Penal Procedure. After consultations in the State Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Croatia, which were based on cooperation between the police and the State Prosecutor's Office in pre-trial and trial proceedings, measures and actions were defined with a view to establish the custody -- the chain of custody of the documents and finding the documents which are property of the Ministry of Defence and which was not in -- submitted to the Main Staff in compliance with the prevailing regulations, and it was not also -- it was also not filed with the central archives. All those documents pertain to Operations Storm and Flash. Those measures also apply to all the other documents that represent archival holdings and also to establishing the crimes which are prosecuted ex officio, the destruction and cover-up of archival holdings, pursuant to Article 327 of the Penal Code of the Republic of Croatia. Likewise, through the implementation plan, people were defined and interviewed. Official Notes were made of all of those interviews. The action plan also describes information which was obtained in the course of those interviews and, based on that, in the follow-up of all those interviews and reports, in -- in the investigation, additional actions were undertaken in order to establish the task force, and those additional actions are as follows: 16 searches of homes and business premises; three searches of passenger vehicles; one search of a lawyer's office; 32 interviews; several thousands of pages of different documents have been seized and are now subject of an in-depth analysis by military experts. As regards Marin Ivanovic, as well as other individuals, in keeping with Article 211 of the Law on Penal Procedure, the police authorities have filed a proposal for the search of the apartments and other premises, as well as of the vehicle to the municipal prosecutor's office in Zagreb. In keeping with Article 211 of the Law on Penal Procedure, in connection with Article 213 and 214 of the same Law, the Prosecutor's office has sent a proposal to the judge in the court in Zagreb with a request to issue an order for the search of the apartment and other premises, as well as the passenger vehicle. The order was issued by the investigating judge of the county court in Zagreb. On the 9th of December, 2009, on the 9th of December, 2009, at 11.35, in the territory of the police administration of Split and Dalmatia county, the police forces found, located and arrested, pursuant to Article 95, paragraph 2, in connection with Article 102, paragraph 2, of the Law on Penal Procedure, in order to implement the order -- the previous order of the investigating judge of the county court in Zagreb, in order to carry out the search of the apartment of Marin Ivanovic, as well as all of his movable property, i.e., of his passenger vehicles. Likewise, when Marin Ivanovic was stopped, it was noticed that he is in possession of three binders with documentation unknown to the arresting officers. On that same day, at 1930, Mr. Marin Ivanovic was brought by the police officers of the administration of Split and Dalmatia county to the police administration of Zagreb county. The passenger vehicle was searched, the one that he was in at the moment when he was arrested. Three binders were found with documents of military origin, and those documents pertained to Operation Storm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. The issue at stake is whether such a search and seizure could take place. Therefore, to describe what was seized, where it's still to be considered whether the seizure and order search, in any way violated any legal provision, seems not to appropriate to me at this very moment. So I appreciate that you set out what happened, but then to describe the content of those folders in public might not be something that the Chamber expects you to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A laptop was also seized. During the search, it was sealed, and without a special order by an investigating judge, that laptop cannot be switched on or searched. If I may be -- if I may emphasise, that laptop was sealed in the presence of Mr. Ivanovic, as well as of the investigating judge. The search of the vehicle finished at 2250. The search of the apartment, the other vehicle, and the lawyer's office was carried out on the following day; on the 10th of December. As the search of the apartment was carried out at his address in Zagreb which is Trnovcica 32, what was found and seized was an agenda or a diary and several CD media and floppy disks. When the other car was searched, no relevant documents were found. The individuals parents' house was also searched in the territory of the Split and Dalmatia county administration in a village called Krstanica. During the search, no relevant documents were found. When the lawyer's office in Zagreb at Selska 46 was searched, no relevant documents were found there. It is hereby emphasised that the lawyer's office is used exclusively by Mr. Ivanovic. It is by no means an office that is used by the entire Gotovina Defence team. The search of the lawyer's team [as interpreted] was carried out by the investigative judge of the -- the search of the lawyer's office was carried out by the investigative judge of the county court in Zagreb, Mrs. Jadranka Mandusic, in the presence of the Croatian Bar Association, Mila Mikecin Misetic, keeping with the law -- provisions of the Law of Legal Profession. After an interview, Mr. Ivanovic was released. The Republic of Croatia would like to emphasise once again that in undertaking all the activities during the administrative investigation and during the activities undertaken by the task force, the constitutional law has been fully compiled with. The constitutional Law on Cooperation with The Hague Tribunal dating back to 1996, as well as all the other Croatian relevant regulations. The same applies to the activities undertaken by the task force which we have just described. Croatia does not oppose to the participation of the State Prosecutor, Mr. Bajic, at the hearing on the 16th of December, should the Trial Chamber deem his presence necessary. As far as the alleged pressures on the part of the OTP on the bodies of the Republic of Croatia, Croatia is prepared to provide the Trial Chamber the complete correspondence between the OTP and the Croatian government, in order to shed even more light on the communication between the two that exist -- that has existed so far. Croatia would like to emphasise that all the undertaken activities, starting with the administrative investigation to the activities of the task force, have been directed towards complying with the order issued by the Trial Chamber on the 16th of December, 2008, as well as the request on the part of the OTP of the ICTY to submit the necessary documents, as well as the need for the Republic of Croatia to locate the missing archival holdings which are its property. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ambassador. Well, you said that we'll find the answers in your statement. Unfortunately, it's not entirely clear. You mentioned quite a lot of legal instruments and some various purposes for seeking documentary evidence. I see at least three options, at least options of these matters, which were referred to by you in any way. The first is the ongoing proceedings against Mr. Ivanovic; another option would be any new investigation or any new proceedings instituted against Mr. Ivanovic; you also quoted the Law on Cooperation with the Tribunal, but that could be another purpose for search and seizure, at least potentially. It is not yet clear to me in what procedural context the search was ordered, was permitted. You said that there were orders sought and orders received. Now, usually on an order you find a number and a name of an accused. If it's a criminal -- or at least an investigation or proceedings under penal law. In administrative matters you might find something else. I do not how the cooperation with the Tribunal is registered, by what type of proceedings. But I'd like to know exactly what -- the context of what proceedings these search and seizures have taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could please activate your mike.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARO
utterances.text: If you allow me, I don't consider myself sufficiently expert on these procedural matters, but maybe Mr. Cule might help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you assisted by him, so his assistance will certainly be useful. Mr. Cule.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Josip Cule. I am the Deputy of the Chief State Prosecutor of the Republic of Croatia. As for searches which have been mentioned in the statement read out by Mr. Ambassador, these were searches ordered by the investigative judge of the relevant court in the Republic of Croatia. Therefore, please -- therefore searches can only be conducted by order of court. There can be no searches without a court order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me clarify how these orders were issued and how the searches were consequently conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your answer, I take it that these were searches conducted in the context of criminal procedure or investigations preceding -- so, penal law rather than administrative law. If that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I got the impression that the witness -- the witness, I'm sorry. That Mr. Cule would -- was about to explain -- and my impression was somewhat different than your's, Mr. President, so perhaps he could explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will ask him to explain. But what I would like to ask him is also to focus on not only the -- the general legal context but also if we're talking about an investigation, that who is the suspect in that investigation, or if it is proceedings taken against a person, who is that person, and on what suspicion exactly, especially whether it's the same subject matter as we have found in the pending case against Mr. Ivanovic, or whether it's anything different from that, either a different person or different events. Please continue. I apologise for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are many questions so I have to start with the last question so that what I said last would be made clearer. There is one proceedings ongoing against Marin Ivanovic, and the proposal of the indictment has been issued. There is another proceedings ongoing against him, where the county court in Zagreb has requested that investigative activities against him be carried out. These investigative activities were requested on the 19th of November, 2009. What the Ambassador just spoke about is relating to the new circumstances. Namely, the task force has established new information that Marin Ivanovic could be in possession of some more documents and, therefore, could have committed another crime under Article 327 of the Penal Code. When the police has information of this kind, then it has to carry out certain investigations when proceeding further. So this is not yet criminal procedure. It is just that there is certain suspicion. One of the activities that can be carried out is also the search of an apartment or of premises or of a vehicle. In order for -- for it to be possible for a search to take place and there is no criminal procedure as yet, the police addresses the State Prosecutor's Office. The State Prosecutor's Office then assesses whether there are sufficient elements in the proposal of the police which make it likely that the investigation would yield some results; that is to say, that certain documents might be found or not. The State Prosecutor's office then requests the court to issue an order for the search of a apartment. So this is still not criminal procedure. This is all part of what we call preliminary investigative procedure. Once the court issues the order to search an apartment, once the search is conducted, and once the State Prosecutor's Office is informed about the results of the police work, the State Prosecutor's Office will only then make a decision whether criminal procedure would be initiated or not. As for information on the basis of the data provided by the task force, the police requested, I think, a total of a search of 19 premises or was it 19 persons? But, in any case, the State Prosecutor's office did not endorse all the proposals of the police. In one case, it was of the opinion that the circumstances stated were not sufficient. So, in this case, the police carried out some activities and then the State Prosecutor's office and the court did so, all of that in connection with new information found through the activities of the task force as explained by the Ambassador in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand now that the searches and the seizures took place in the recently initiated preliminary investigative procedures, which are directed against Mr. Ivanovic. Is Mr. Ivanovic the only suspect in that case or are there more suspects?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he is not the only one. There are several persons. I believe that the report that has been submitted mentions these persons individually, and I think that there are eight in number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm primarily interested in whether or not there are any other members of any of the Defence teams in this case included in the other suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, have I the name of these persons here. I don't know if I can read all these names of these persons publicly. I have them here. It's a document which was submitted to the ICTY. It's a report to the Trial Chamber and the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dated?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know if -- Dated the 9th of November, 2009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's mainly for you to consider whether or not it would be appropriate to pronounce these names in public. I'm mainly interested - and another way of dealing with the matter would be - that Mr. Misetic could confirm or deny that there's any other Defence team member involved. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before anyone considers the procedure of reading those names out loud, I believe if I understand the date correctly that information is already available to the Defence and the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, of course, the Chamber has asked the Republic of Croatia to report. That does not mean that we're always analysing the reports submitted in such a way that the transparency in what we know and what we do not know is lost. We'll use that material in accordance with the matters that are put to us; that is, satisfaction or lack of satisfaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I may have missed an exchange with you and Mr. Misetic. I was just suggesting that rather than hear the names and then compare it to members of the Defence team, that Mr. Misetic could look at the report and then advise the Court whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that was what you intended, I think I already hinted at that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's 358 pages, so if I could ask build Cule's assistance in finding the right page in the report, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And the second thing just for -- just to be cautious, the report itself, Croatia has made confidential so that we don't discuss it in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is mentioned by Mr. Cule, and I think merely mentioning it might not be prejudicial, but -- it's the -- if it's confidential, then it's the interests of the Republic of Croatia which are in the foreground so ... Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm -- I'm confused --

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please allow me before we go on. The document has been taken from me. I thought that it was for the needs of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what we wanted to do, as a matter of fact, is to invite Mr. Misetic to check in that document whether he finds the names of any other members of his team, and then it will be returned to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. President, I obviously have a problem --

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think as far as I have seen from this report, which has three or four pages, only one person is mentioned as a possible former member of a lawyer's team. There is only one person with such a note in this report, but we can see that immediately when Mr. Misetic has it now and is reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see two members of my team and a third former member which is consistent with what happened on Wednesday. I also note that the report is -- the caption of the report is the same that was filed on the 9th November, but the information in this report contains information about what happened on Wednesday as well as the 7th of December. So this appears to be something that is not yet filed with the parties in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first purpose, that is, to identify whether there are more members of the Gotovina Defence team involved, is herewith served. I invite to you give it to Mr. Usher so that it can be returned to Mr. Cule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I do not know how familiar you are with the composition of the Markac Defence team, but whether you found any one, because we have a kind of a -- of a subsidiary concerns. But perhaps that could be resolved also during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would not speak for the Markac Defence, Mr. President, because I don't know all of their members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but that seems to be less on the foreground at this moment. But I just do not want to forget about the interests of the Markac Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we have -- I have a few more questions. 16 searches of homes and businesses, as was reported. I understood that to be the searches conducted a couple of days ago. Now, homes and businesses, were that homes of any members of the Gotovina Defence team, were they included, and if so were they also homes and businesses of persons not being members of the Gotovina Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I just say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cule, if you would not mind Mr. Misetic, when he is on his feet, it usually helps us, so, therefore, I don't want to be rude to you, but first before asking you to answer the question to hear what Mr. Misetic could add.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just -- I'm sorry to interrupt, Mr. President, in light of the witness's -- again, I'm sorry, in light of Mr. Cule's last response, he may not be aware of two of the individuals on the list. So in addition to Mr. Ivanovic, we assert that Jozo Ribicic is a member of the Gotovina Defence and Mr. Hucic is a former member of the Gotovina Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say that allows -- that enables Mr. Cule to answer the question. Were there -- were the homes and businesses of Mr. Ribicic and, I think it was Mr. Hucic, are they on the list as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the information of the persons that have been mentioned as members of the Defence team, in addition to what is mentioned in relation to Marin Ivanovic, the search of the apartment of Zeljko Hucic has been carried out at the address in Zagreb, a certain address in Zagreb, and also of the persons who are listed, the search of the home, to call it that way, of Mr. Jozo Ribicic in Split, in Simiceva street, and on that occasion, his personal computer was also seized. And on the basis of a separate order of the investigative judge, the computer was also searched. To make this additionally clear, another separate judge's order is needed for a computer search to be conducted. As for other searches and other premises, I do not have information whether any of these persons are members of any Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Or related to them, because I heard that the parental home of Mr. Ivanovic was searched as well. So it might be difficult at this moment to identify if there are any further family relations involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Maybe I would be of some assistance if I could be able to see the list, just to inform the Chamber whether some of the Markac team members is also ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to Mr. Cule. If would you be willing to give the list to Mr. Mikulicic, then that might resolve an additional question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no doubts whether I can provide it to Mr. Mikulicic, because when Mr. Misetic saw it, it would be very dangerous if I did not provide it to my colleague Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would be please assist in temporarily handing over the document to Mr. Mikulicic. It was explained that in the search of the law firm that a representative of the Croatian Bar Association was present. Could you explain what the role of that is and whether there's a legal basis for his presence during such a search?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When a lawyer's office is searched, one has to meet the requirements of a special procedure. Namely, a search of a lawyer's office has to be attended by the investigative judge who issued the order for the search or another person designated by them. Likewise, the Bar Association has to be informed, as the Bar Association is going to send its representative, pursuant to the provisions of Article 17 on legal profession. In case the procedure is not followed, the evidence obtained in such a way would be considered invalid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, does that procedure apply exclusively when the search takes place in the law firm; or would such a procedure also apply if you find a lawyer on the street with his suitcase? So would it apply to any seizure of matters, which are in possession of a lawyer; or would it be limited to the premises where his office is located?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The law is clear. It says when it comes to the search of a lawyer, or a lawyer's office, which implies to the physical search of a lawyer or their office, including vehicles and other such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that when the car of Mr. Ivanovic, in which he transported, apparently, orders -- binders, and a -- and a computer, that a representative of the Bar Association was present at that moment as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment when the vehicle property of Marin Ivanovic was seized from him, it was sealed. And as far as I know, it was transported on a special truck - I don't know the exact name of the vehicle - all the way to the police station in Zagreb, in order to be searched in the prescribed way. Which means that it was not searched on the spot and so far the -- the contents of the laptop have not been searched, since there is still no order for such a search in place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what about the apartments of the three members of the Gotovina Defence team just mentioned? The searches in their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are private individuals. And as far as they are concerned, they are subject to the provisions of the Law on Penal Procedure. Whenever such a search is carried out, two persons have to be present during the search, as well as the suspect, and the suspect has the right to the presence of a lawyer. And allow me to explain, because I am afraid that it has been registered incorrectly in the transcript. When we are talking about private individuals, about individuals who are not lawyers or members of the legal profession, regular provisions of the Law on Penal Procedure are applied in the way that I have just described, which means that only one person of all of those who have been subject of this investigation and searches only one, according to our information, is a representative of the legal profession and that is Marin Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My next question would be: Does the legal privilege extend to those who are employed and are directly involved in the work of members of the legal profession? Secretaries, such people. Those who are assisting the member of the legal profession in his activities, in his professional activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please clarify? Are you referring to the privileges that are extended to the confidentiality clause that applies to lawyers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question would be to -- to give an example, that, if a lawyer asks his secretary to -- or someone else to assist him in investigations, that person not being a member of the legal profession himself but when he's carrying, for example, notes he has made of interviews with potential witnesses or with the accused, or the suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have before me the Law on The Legal Profession and in its Article 17, entitled search of lawyers and law offices, and that Article does not mention anything about the personnel in the lawyer's office. The Article only explains how lawyers and lawyers' offices will be searched. But there is one part of the Article that I'm going read from, and I believe that that part will be of some assistance. When it comes to the search of a lawyer or a lawyer's office, the confidentiality and secrecy of documents should not be violated or any of the other objects at the detriment of the parties. At this moment, I am not aware of the judicial practices as to how should the other persons that you have mentioned in your question should be treated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's, then, focus, to start with, on the seizure in the law firm and the seizure of matters which were in Mr. Ivanovic's car. Mr. Misetic, you were on your feet a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes just to give you an additional fact concerning the car. I am advised by Mr. Ivanovic that the -- I believe there was reference to military documents in his car. Mr. Ivanovic advises me that it's approximately 400 to 500 pages, all of them - every piece of paper - was an OTP document with an ERN number on it and that the Croatian authorities were advised. And as far as I'm concerned, they are still subject to the Court's 14th July 2006 order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, as you may have noticed I sought not to further explore at that moment the exact -- the exact -- the content of the material, because that would not lead us, at this moment, very far. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, slight intervention as it refers to the transcript. Page 28, line 11. Mr. Cule cited the paragraph 17th of the according law. And there was a word "stranka" mentioned in the original Croatian language which was translated as parties. Although we are not in possession like we used to be when witness is testifying, I should emphasise that that word "stranka" in that context should be translated as "client," not parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whereas it also has the meaning of party, "stranka," because I remember the name of one of the permanent parties in the former Yugoslavia to contain the word "stranka" in its title. Thank you. Mr. Cule, you said that searches should not violate the legal privilege. Now, who decides what falls within the scope of privileged material and is not within the scope of the privileged material?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The results of the research [as interpreted] or the result of the investigation and everything that has been seized is in the hands of the court. On several occasions, during each procedure the court takes decisions on the validity of the evidence, and any of the parties may challenge the validity of the search warrant, the minutes of the search that was carried out, or the record of such a search. And it will be the Court that will eventually make the decision on the validity of any of the evidence. There's also the right to appeal against all that, and any such appeal, again, is decided by the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if the court decides on the validity of the evidence, may I then take it that the parties, both parties, have access to that material already before the court gives any decision on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that I understood the question properly. I will still answer, and then if there is something missing from my answer, I suppose will you have additional questions. The search warrant, before any action is taken, is handed to the suspect in question and to his legal representative, if he has one. The record of the search is signed, or not, if he doesn't wish to sign it; the suspect, as well as the two persons who were present during the search, and also the record is handed over to the suspect once it is signed. Which means that throughout the entire procedure -- I suppose that I have misunderstood the question after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to focus my question. Perhaps by way of an example. You enter a law firm. You seize five binders. Now the lawyer present says, Three out of these five is material which falls within the scope of my legal privilege; that is, it is stuff I can confidentially communicate with my clients and that is the stuff you will find in these three binders. Binder number 1 are some articles I've ever written. Binder 2 is my bookkeeping. But these three, are privileged. Who then decides who looked into those binders to decide whether or not they should be exempted from seizure? Because seizure would, or might violate, the legal privilege.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must admit, that I have never been in a similar situation. When a search of a lawyer or his office takes place, a judge has to be present. And always when a judge is present during an investigative procedure, such as, for example, the site investigation of a traffic accident, the judge has the final say. If the judge says that something will not be seized, or that something will not be carried out or done, I'm sure that it will not happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the mere presence of a judge, of course, is not yet an answer to the issue. You said it never happened to you. I must admit, that, in my past, I have been present during some searches and it's not easy, especially in a law firm where you could expect a lot of confidential communication to be in almost all of the files, to identify what is protected by legal privilege and what is not protected by legal privilege. The mere fact that a judge is there, who, I take it, will not be able to go through the hard disks of all these computers, who will not be able to go through all these files and read them all in all -- in order to find out what is privileged material or not. So, therefore, I hear your answer, but I still do not fully understand, unless the situation is that a judge says, Well, is this privileged? We leave it here, because you say so. Or, is it privileged we'll, nevertheless, take it with us, because we could not just rely on what are you're telling us. I mean, the mere presence of a judge might not be the clue to a -- to a observance of legal privilege in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The presence of a judge also means his duty. A judge provides the ultimate guarantee that a law will be observed. A judge does not make his decision based on what somebody says, but, rather, based on his own judgement about everything that he has learned so far. This is, indeed, a very difficult and hypothetical question as well. And I believe that only a person who participated in an investigation on site is in a position to tell you why they reached a certain decision and why not another decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm rather not talking about -- not taking responsibility for decisions. I'm mainly talking about impossibility of checking a hard disk within perhaps even one day. That's my concern, that if you would, in detail, review, whether a matter falls within or outside the scope of a legal privilege, that that's perhaps very difficult to be done on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that that is one of the reasons why a representative of the Bar Association has to be present as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I earlier asked you what exactly his role was. I do understand that it's the judge who decides. What is the role of the representative of the Bar Association?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that -- that he has to be there as professional colleague who can also set boundaries of confidentiality, and in that way, assist the judge, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we find the specific provisions for search in law firms environment or lawyers? Do we find them in 211, 213, and 214? Because you quoted -- you mentioned these articles although it was not entirely clear to me whether these articles were the specific ones to protect privileged information or whether they were the articles which would, in a more general way, give the proceedings -- give the procedure for search and seizure.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Law on Penal Procedure explains the so-called regular procedure. And there is a special law, the Law on Legal Profession, in its Article 17, which regulates the way searches are carried out of a -- lawyers and their offices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could anyone, either you, Mr. Cule, or any of the parties, assist the Chamber in providing Article 17 of this law? It may be that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you could -- I take it that you have it in your own language?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will check. I may have it in English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cule.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I don't have it in English. I have it only in Croatian, and I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If, nevertheless, you could provide it to us, and I take it that you have it electronically. But there are ways to send it to the Registry perhaps so that we will find a solution for that -- a practical solution for that soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can do it this very moment, if somebody has a memory stick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anyone, or have you all lost your memory sticks as is the tradition in many legal environments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I found it on the Internet, on the web site, and I can send the link to Mr. Registrar so that will help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have it from two sources. Nevertheless, thank you, Mr. Cule. But they've all lost their memory sticks. There is a very specific problem in the present context, which is the following. From your words and from the context you have described, I think we could not exclude for the possibility that you have in the back of your mind that if you would find in any of the seized materials, any document the Prosecution is seeking, that you will consider to hand that over to the Tribunal. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This creates the very specific problem of whether the guarantees, the guarantees not to violate what is within the scope of legal privilege, whether that would be construed and is regulated in Croatia in the same manner as the ICTY would -- would construe, in procedural terms, what the obligations are. That is, who defines what is privileged; what are the consequences of any violation of legal privilege. It is, as a matter of fact, a problem which is known from the past, that if obtaining evidence or transferring evidence from one jurisdiction to another is at stake, that the question arises whether the rules are congruent, or are not congruent, which may have an effect on the use of evidence. I'm expressing myself in very general terms at this moment. I'm asking this, because it may be clear that, as you reported, you have done whatever you're supposed to do under Croatian law. At the same time, it may be that the Tribunal would require more - we still have to consider that - or less, if it ever comes to transferring any such material to the Tribunal. I'm not asking at this moment a very concrete answer, but would the Republic of Croatia consider to temporarily freeze all the material which is seized and further discuss with the Tribunal whether any additional checking, any additional check, on the possibility of a violation of legal privilege would take place? For example, it's -- it's a matter which has not been further explored, but I'm just trying to understand, for example, to give a role to -- give a role to the panel which deals with such -- well, at least -- who deals with matters in relation to the functioning of the legal profession before this Tribunal. I'm referring to -- I'm asking you, whether, for example, an involvement of the advisory panel which consists of five members appointed by national bar organisations, or four out of them being appointed by the International Bar Association and the Union Internationale des Avocats, whether -- would you be willing to consider a check on any violation of confidentiality? I can imagine that you do not have immediately an answer, but is that something to which you say no -- there's a no, this is not something we could consider or -- and that would then, of course, first require that that no further activity would then be undertaken in relation to that material, that it should be sealed, as the one computer is already sealed, and then to wait for a while and to see whether a procedure could be worked out which would satisfy not only Croatian law but also -- and I must say, underdeveloped law in this respect in this Tribunal, because we do not have much case law on this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could say I would like to consider this during the break, then the question has been put to you. We need to have a break anyhow soon, and it may that you want to consult with whomever. So but that question is -- is then there. If you would need further information about the composition of the advisory panel -- and I'm not saying that the advisory panel would consider this to be within their responsibilities, but at least the thought has come up for any procedural solution for the problem I just described. And, of course, I'm also inviting the parties, and you could then include any responses to such a question by the parties when considering to answer my question. Mr. Misetic, I have -- I have -- as a matter of fact, I've got two questions for you. First of all, one question is for the Prosecution; the other is for you, Mr. Misetic. Would you agree, or would you consider if evidential material, material which may have been material to the commission of an offence, is kept by counsel or in his -- in the premises of his law firm, that that would be inappropriate to keep it there, where it would be shielded against search and seizure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand, but I think my position is that that question depends on from what perspective you approach it. I think it's fundamentally clear that lawyers generally cannot engage in crime and that there should be procedures in place so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about lawyers being engaged in crime. Let me give a simple example. A client comes and -- has the knife with which as was -- as he was suspected to have done, with which he had killed his neighbour six weeks ago, comes and says, Could you please keep this for me. It's evidence. We shouldn't lose it. Keep it in your office. Then, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You cannot -- you absolutely cannot keep that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You cannot keep that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In my submission, and as far as I understand, the ethical duties in my own jurisdiction, no you cannot, that circumstance, keep the weapon and conceal it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is because it is important evidence for --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is, in some respects, in our jurisdiction, you could consider it obstruction of justice. It would be -- well, I would argue under our rules here in the Tribunal, a potential Rule 77 contempt proceedings, which is how I was going to -- why I said it depends on from what perspective you approach this. I believe the Tribunal absolutely has jurisdiction to deal with matters and cases that are in front of it. There is a multiple layer of this which I had hoped and continued to hope to be able to address with the Chamber today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not ready yet today, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I know. But the question becomes, is this simply a matter of Croatian law applying its laws to this problem or if, in fact, it turns out that this is being done pursuant to an organ of this Tribunal, particularly the Prosecution in this case, then I don't believe the Trial Chamber can simply relegate it to how Croatian authority will apply Croatian law because this Trial Chamber is seized with, under Article 20, sub para 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- applying the rules to both parties in this case. If there is a reason to believe - and I will state this on the record - if the Prosecution in this case has information that would say, That the knife is in possession of one of the Defence team, I don't think there is any question that the Trial Chamber can issue an order saying, Produce the knife. But there has to be some basis -- some evidentiary basis for that. You can't just then say, I can't establish with the Trial Chamber that the knife is with you, so I'm going to have the police search through your office to see if the knife is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is all based on highly disputed factual background. We've heard that we can receive all the correspondence between the Prosecutor's office and since -- at least that is certainly a matter which we will not conclude to look at today. But you say whether or not one of the parties in the proceedings has triggered or encouraged to -- to seize that material without an order, and if that would be Tribunal parties, that that's your view, that you couldn't then seek to have that seized without -- without any order from the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but, Mr. President, I think we have here a situation: Mr. Cule has indicated that they got a warrant from a judge in Zagreb. I believe for a Defence team at the ICTY, whatever information was used to obtain the warrant should have been produced to Trial Chamber for the Trial Chamber then to authorise such a warrant or such a procedure. If that is, in fact, the bottom line. Because if evidence exists of that, I haven't seen it, and I have repeatedly -- even on the record what the Trial Chamber said, we have done our own investigations into this and have not found - and have no reason to believe that we are in possession of - documents which are sought pursuant to the RFA at issue here. If there is evidence that would be sufficient for the Chamber to authorise such a search, then I would submit this it should be brought to the Chamber. The Chamber should review it and should issue an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say that apart from -- if the Chamber orders that documents should be produced, or at least should investigated whether they can be found, that, nevertheless, in every time, when -- for achieving that purpose, it would be needed to search in order to be able to seize, that this Chamber should issue always an order in that respect, so that in --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the Chamber would be involved in the details of the execution of an earlier order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me take it step by step. We have a precedent in this case already. The Prosecution filed a -- essentially a request to produce documents but in the form of a motion seeking an order for us to produce categories of documents that were there. The Chamber's ultimate ruling - and I need to be careful here because ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say it may be confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'm not positive. Can we move into private session. I believe it is confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can move into private session, but we have to stop because the tapes are running out very quickly at this moment. What I would like after the break to, first of all, to hear from the representatives of the Republic of Croatia whether any further checking of any seized material, whether that would be debatable. I'm not in a debate but, at least, what their position would be, and would like to -- of course, the Prosecution also, to think about this possibility, because this -- the problem we have in front of us consists of many, many aspects, and this is one of them on which I would like to focus at this moment. We have to have a break, because, otherwise, our words will be lost forever. Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. CULE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I could just say something that would not be in the record, as the Defence attorney said that the Republic of Croatia is only acting on the request of the Prosecutor's office --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may say it after the break, but in 15 seconds the tape will be expiring. And, therefore, we adjourn, and we resume at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a bit of a late start. We were informed that you had a consultation with your government. Before we continue, I'd first like to put on the record that, something with the external line feed is not properly functioning. So even if it is difficult to have access to these proceedings at this very moment, reason unknown, there are no conspiracies. The video of this hearing will be made available anyhow. Of course, to the extent it's public, and it was entirely public until now. So, therefore, just to put this on the record, that it may be difficult to follow these proceedings at this very moment, but everybody will be made available. One small question to start with. Mr. Mikulicic, did you identify any person on the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not on that list that was provided to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's, then, on the record as well. Yes, I would to now invite the parties to -- in this case, the Prosecution, to briefly respond to what is the core of what we're dealing with this afternoon. That is, a -- a kind of freezing order, to say so. If there's any problem with that. Freezing would mean? Freezing to further inspect the assets under the -- the seized matters; that would be documents, hard disks, computers, whatever is seized at this moment, until we have further considered the various aspects of the present situation, and we are focussing, at this moment, primarily on client/counsel privilege, as being the first at stake. Of course, there's the confidentiality of other material which may be about protective witnesses. That is what we're focussing on at this moment. And we'd like to hear from the Prosecution whether what their position is in relation to such a motion. Mr. Misetic, is there any need to further explain? It may be clear that freezing just means keeping your options open and see what the next steps would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I rose only because I don't know which would be more efficient. I obviously have -- I would say a 20 to 30 minute response -- a reply both to the Prosecution and the Croatian position, because there are substantial portions with which we disagree and think will put things in the proper context. But, obviously, if there's a specific narrow question that you're asking the Prosecution, that's fine. But, especially in light of how the first session went, I think there is -- are broader issues that need to be raised with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the Prosecution has responded in writing to the first written motion. What I'm seeking at this moment is specifically the position of the Prosecution, which is not primarily about who triggered what because that is -- that is dealt with, whether satisfactorily or not is a different matter. The parties may have different views on that, but that's dealt with in the filing we received this morning. At this moment, I'm primarily now seeking the position of the Prosecution to -- for this moment to issue an order, and that's what was asked, whether we'll do it or not, Mr. Ambassador, is still to be considered by this Chamber, but what the Prosecution's position would be, that at this moment, the -- this material, that is documentary material and other material, would not be further inspected until further order, and then we would, of course, look rather quickly to all the remaining elements of which we have dealt with only in a very limited way until now. And just to say there, of course, there may be several aspects in this as well. That is, is it within our competence, within our jurisdiction, if you have any views on that, why it would be or would not be, of course, the Chamber would like to hear, and, of course, the substance of the order itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I thank you. I'm going to begin with the narrowest possible response, and we'll take it from there, I think. And that is, from the Prosecution's point of view in -- in terms of the instant -- the matter before the Trial Chamber, undertaking what I understand to the court's suggestion from that point of view, that is, do we have an objection to stopping for a brief time, not receiving any -- I mean, from our point of view it would be not receiving any materials. It wouldn't be anything affirmative or anything, so from the Prosecution's point of view if we have an objection to not receiving any materials resulting from the search from Croatia until the court and the parties have been given an opportunity to address this issue fairly, no, we don't have an objection to that. In fact, that's contrary. We would not want the court to proceed precipitously in -- in any direction on a significant matter to affect the rights of either party or the institution generally. Or Croatia, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you think it would be within the competence, within the jurisdiction of this Chamber to issue such an order?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You know -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I know, exactly. I think as a general matter, Your Honour, from the limited opportunity that I've had to review the jurisprudence, I -- I don't see the -- see it -- necessarily see the Tribunal's competence to make orders with respect to a domestic criminal investigation. I don't think the Tribunal could order someone, for example, order the Croatian authorities, to investigate a specific person, indict a specific person, prosecute a specific person and soon on. Now, that's the preliminary and I know that's the spirit in which the Court has made the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But I also say I'm not sure that, and before we go down that road and start debating those competences in more limited context, or indeed in broader context, it appears to me that that may not be at issue here. I mean, for one thing, if the Prosecution doesn't -- is -- is agreeable to not acceptable material for the limited period we've discussed until the matter has been thrashed out, I'm a little hard pressed to see -- I mean, now, you've still got the question of other forms of dissemination of the material presumably, but I'm not aware yet that the Court has explored with the Croatian authorities the possibility of arriving that solution, at that temporary abeyance, absent the necessity of a formal order and an examination of the competence to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for that answer. You're clear on that you do not oppose against not receiving material for a while. You're clear on that. Then, in respect of the competence of this Chamber to issue orders, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah. We simply haven't done sufficient level of research. The preliminary indication is as I indicated, but it would be remiss of me to suggest that I a definitive answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. We are all trying to form our opinions on rather complex matters in a very quick way, and I think everyone is struggling with that. Mr. Misetic, could we hear about your struggle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that -- that the Chamber's jurisdiction to issue such orders is clear under the case law and under the Statute. And I -- by way of an example explain why. If we take the situation that there is a witness who testified here, let's say, we are aware that the Croatian authorities are conducting investigations into, let's take, for an example, Varivode, if a witness has come here and testified with full protective measures about Varivode, could a Croatian investigative judge compel Mr. Ivanovic to disclose the name or papers so that that investigation in Croatia could proceed with more information as to the identity of the witness that testified, who may have testified with pseudonym and face distortion but in public and the judge thought there was valuable testimony that could be gained by this. I think the answer would be quite clearly no. The Trial Chamber's orders for protection take precedent. We, as the Defence, would have an obligation to the Chamber, first and foremost, and couldn't simply say there is a parallel investigation going, and we also have an obligation to, essentially, violate an order of the Chamber. I don't see any material distinction between an order of the Chamber and a rule or the Statute. In other words, if something is precluded by, for example, the code of professional conduct at the ICTY, that may be lawful, for example, disclosing a client confidence, because an investigative judge in Croatia wants it. I believe that counsel could be disciplined at the ICTY because we're bounds by the code of professional conduct here. So I believe that the Tribunal in keeping matters directly related to it has the jurisdiction and authority to enforce its own orders, and similarly must have, by implication, the jurisdiction to enforce both the rules and rules which flow from Article 21 of the Statute. I think the Appeals Chamber's jurisprudence has been clear that the attorney/client and work product privileges flow from the accused's right under Article 21 against self-incrimination. If the Chamber did not have jurisdiction to enforce those rights and rules, then obviously they're not worth very much, and I think that implicit in the jurisprudence and in the jurisdiction of the Chamber is obviously the power to enforce its own orders, rules, and the rights of the accused. So to that extent we would say that if the Chamber were to find that both attorney/client work product matters could be disclosed as well as matters which are currently governed by orderings of the Chamber, and by way of example, the documents seized in Mr. Ivanovic's car are documents disclosed by OTP to us and which are still under an order of the 14th of July 2006, we would say that obviously the Chamber must have the authority to enforce the 14 July 2006 order as well as the rights guaranteed under the Statute. In terms of -- I appreciate Mr. Tieger's position with respect to information being received by the Prosecution but that still leaves us in the position that persons in Croatia could search the laptop, the hard drives, et cetera, and continue with further investigative steps. For example, I will disagree with Mr. Cule that one office that isn't related to the Gotovina Defence was searched. That office is related. I have been there personally myself. There is obviously nothing to preclude the Croatian authorities from conducting a search of the second office. So while none of that information ultimately will go to the Prosecution under the position taken by the Prosecution, that still doesn't prevent the injury, because the question is not only is the attorney/client privilege protect from disclosure to the Prosecution, it protects from the disclosure to essentially to anyone and it should be. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, then, now I have some more thoughts as a result of this responsive dialogue, Your Honour, and I hope -- and again the Court needs to let us know when -- and there's a certain level of brain-storming and spontaneity of this happening. If you've heard enough, let me know. I'm not trying to intrude unnecessarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. If you say that -- you're telling us that you have developed some thoughts, the Chamber is always interested in hearing any thoughts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I -- again, the first thing I was going to say, first of all, we know that the Court has already indicated it should only intrude in exceptional circumstances. That's fairly consonant with the general rule of least restrictive measures, least intrusive measures. I don't think that's really at issue. Mr. Misetic is -- seems to be suggesting that where the possibility exists that some violation of confidentiality may occur, the Court should take the measure that it would take in the face of information that it was about to occur or had been occurring. That does not strike me as the least intrusive measure. Secondly, the last example provided by Mr. Misetic seems to focus not on the -- on the -- a general issue of confidentiality not related to materials before this Court but seemingly related to Croatia's investigation to obtain its own documents. Now, first of all, I don't think this Court has a particular -- has particular standing or interest to supervise the practices of judicial systems generally for their own purposes. So where this matter strays into areas of investigation that are being pursued by Croatia under its own domestic jurisprudence by Croatian officials under Croatian law to seek Croatian documents, that's a separate matter. The question is at what point does the court's interest in the -- the privilege take hold.
